title: Rorca Supabase Database and Credential Authority Adapter

acceptanceCriteria: Binding preflight rejects wrong project/database/environment, stale generation, unverified role, missing capabilities, and unresolved references
Schema inspection executes read-only and returns a deterministic inventory with stable object identifiers and hashes
Inspect cannot execute DDL, DML, backup, restore, migration, key rotation, or provider administration
Application anon/publishable/secret/service credentials do not grant database schema or migration authority
Responses, receipts, logs, and database authority rows contain connection/key references and fingerprints but no credential bytes
userStories.description: Implement a generic Supabase database AuthorityProviderAdapter and ProviderBinding for one project/environment using immutable project reference, database identity, verified role/capability profile, binding generation, and SecretStore references. database.schema.inspect returns tables, columns, constraints, indexes, extensions, functions, and RLS policies through read-only transactions. Use core authority storage; add no provider-specific secret column. Staging and production bindings are separate and no application runtime credential implies migration authority.
userStories.title: Supabase bindings expose exact read-only schema inventory

acceptanceCriteria: Backup creation produces a verifiable encrypted artifact record with hash, source identity, retention, and no embedded credential
A scratch restore recreates expected schema/data checks and records target identity and verification evidence
Restore rejects ambiguous, source-equal, production, stale, or unauthorized targets before writing
Inspect and backup grants cannot authorize restore or migration operations
Backup or restore crash reconciles provider/storage state and leaves one receipt or an explicit cleanup-required record
userStories.description: Implement database.backup.create and database.backup.restore as distinct capabilities. Create records provider/storage location, content hash, schema/version metadata, encryption provenance, retention, and verification result. Restore requires explicit target identity, scratch by default, a separate high-risk grant, and post-restore integrity checks. Production restore is unavailable without a separately reviewed policy and external gate.
userStories.title: Backup evidence and target verification protect restore drills

acceptanceCriteria: Preflight rejects schema-hash drift, missing or reordered migrations, duplicate ids, dependency conflicts, unsupported transaction mode, and absent recovery classification
Reversible staging migration failure executes its tested rollback and verifies the prior schema state
Forward-only staging migration failure follows the declared forward-fix or scratch-restore procedure and records the resulting schema hash
Concurrent and replayed apply attempts cannot double-apply a migration manifest
The receipt records manifest digest, target identity, before/after schema hashes, statements outcome, verification, and recovery proof without credentials
userStories.description: Implement database.migration.apply.staging from an immutable ordered manifest containing ids, content hashes, current-schema hash, prerequisites, transaction mode, reversibility classification, verification queries, and rollback or forward-fix procedure. Do not require a fictitious down script for every migration: reversible migrations provide tested rollback; forward-only migrations provide backup, forward-fix, and restore evidence. Apply under an advisory/fencing lock, verify expected schema state, and settle a receipt.
userStories.title: Staging migration preflight preserves exact ordering and recovery policy

acceptanceCriteria: Production apply rejects missing/failed backup, changed manifest/schema, closed window, invalid external gate, expired/replayed grant, and unverified recovery plan
Deployment authority cannot call production migration operations and production migration authority cannot call deploy operations
The exact backup, manifest, target, window, evidence, and recovery owner are bound to the grant digest
Crash before, during, or after apply reconciles schema/history before retry and never double-applies a manifest
Abort follows the declared reversible rollback, forward-fix, or restore path and records final database consistency
userStories.description: Implement database.migration.apply.production with immutable manifest and target digests, verified backup, change window, health/abort evidence, rollback owner, and external gate when policy requires independent approval. A deploy grant cannot authorize database mutation and a migration grant cannot deploy application code. Preserve WAITING states without consuming story timeout. Reconcile uncertain DDL outcome from schema and migration history before retry.
userStories.title: Production migration authority stays separate from deployment authority

acceptanceCriteria: The API catalog and receipts expose three distinct ceremony types and cannot interchange their grants
Dashboard-created secret and signing values travel directly from secure operator capture to SecretStore/target binding without entering model or ordinary response bodies
Legacy migration inventories every bound consumer and proves replacement before legacy revocation
JWT signing rotation enforces standby, current, and revoked states and verifies old/new token behavior during zero-downtime cutover
Old secret/signing material is revoked only after the exact replacement canary and rollback readiness pass
userStories.description: Implement separate typed ceremonies for publishable/secret API-key rotation, legacy anon/service_role migration, and JWT signing-key standby/current/revoked rotation. Human Dashboard steps use a secure operator capture directly into SecretStore and RuntimeSecretBindingAdapter; values never pass through model chat, ordinary API JSON, or receipts. Each ceremony has its own capability, request digest, binding inventory, canary, cutover, grace/revocation policy, and recovery procedure. Public publishable values are classified separately from server-only secrets.
userStories.title: Distinct Supabase key ceremonies preserve their different blast radii

acceptanceCriteria: Read-only and scratch-restore qualification succeeds before any staging mutation capability is enabled
Reversible and forward-only failure fixtures each end in the declared consistent schema state with complete evidence
Altered manifest, replay, cross-workspace/environment use, deploy-grant substitution, and credential extraction all fail
Crash injection never double-applies a migration, loses a created key, or leaves an untracked binding generation
No Categoric/Cashflow-App database, key, environment, migration, or product code is used
userStories.description: Qualify against a disposable Rorca-owned Supabase project or equivalent supported fixture, never a customer workspace. Exercise read-only inspection, backup/scratch restore, staging reversible and forward-only manifests, separately gated production simulation, all three key-ceremony state machines, replay, cross-scope denial, prompt extraction, and crashes around every external boundary. Rollout proceeds inspect-only, backup/restore, staging mutation, then production/key capabilities. Rollback disables mutation capabilities, revokes leases, and preserves receipts.
userStories.title: Disposable database failures leave one consistent reconciled state
